chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'A drinker of wine, do not marry to him when he proposes'.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marrying a wine drinker in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) conveys the Prophet’s (PBUH) ruling that a khamr-drinker is ineligible for marriage proposals, reflecting the Shia juristic view that habitual intoxication constitutes a major moral defect (fusuq) affecting religious reliability. This ruling underscores the importance of character assessment (khitbah) in Islamic marriage, where the potential spouse's piety and stability are prioritized to ensure a stable family unit.
